'''MWALI''' (<code>0x864E262818C773D3EEC272c2A6A2C8195af1D977</code>) is the [[Proof of Liquidity|proof-of-liquidity]] token on [[PRANA Blockchain|PRANA]]. It exists to reward and measure the liquidity that backs [[KulaSwap|KULA]]. KULA is the reward token; MWALI is the liquidity token. They are deliberately not the same thing.

An earlier MWALI was deployed at <code>0x36C6921e2CECe9DEc7a5AAC42bC6738011F2a1c9</code>. '''That one was never minted and its supply is still zero'''; it is abandoned, and a balance lookup against it will mislead you. The live token is the address above.

== Who can mint it ==

MWALI has exactly one minting role and it is held by a contract, not a person: the MWALI gauge at <code>0x98d0AF33C78133Ae7791330B7a28034ce85AbB59</code>. <code>getRoleMemberCount(MINTER_ROLE)</code> returns '''1''' and <code>getRoleMember(MINTER_ROLE, 0)</code> is that gauge.

Administration belongs to '''nobody'''. <code>getRoleMemberCount(DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE)</code> returns '''0''' — not the operator, not the deployer, not a timelock. A single wiring contract deployed the token, the gauge and the [[KULA Lottery|lottery]] together, granted the gauge the only minting role, and renounced its own admin before that transaction ended. Because no admin exists, '''a second minter can never be added'''. An earlier revision of this page said administration sat behind a two-day DAO timelock; that was true of the superseded token, not this one.

== Five pairs earn it, not one ==

Liquidity providers stake their LP position in the gauge and MWALI is minted to them per second. The emission splits across every live KULA pair by weight, then pro-rata by stake inside each pair, so a smaller pool still earns:

{| class="wikitable"
! Pair !! Weight !! MWALI/sec
|-
| KULA / WPRANA || 50 || 0.005
|-
| KULA / wVKBT || 20 || 0.002
|-
| wCURE / KULA || 20 || 0.002
|-
| wCURE / wVKBT || 5 || 0.0005
|-
| KULA / wMELEK || 5 || 0.0005
|}

The pair list and the weights are '''fixed at construction and immutable'''. Nobody can add a pair, change a weight or redirect the emission. An earlier revision of this page said MWALI was minted only by the KULA/WPRANA gauge; that was the single-pair design, which has been replaced.

== Supply is bounded ==

{| class="wikitable"
| Rate || 0.01 MWALI/sec across all pairs
|-
| Year one || 315,360 MWALI
|-
| Decay || −10% per year
|-
| Lifetime emission || 3,153,600
|-
| Hard cap || 3,468,960
|}

The cap is enforced '''in the token''', not in the gauge — a cap that lives only in the emitter is not a cap, because swapping the emitter removes the ceiling. Burned supply is not re-mintable either: the cap counts everything ever minted, so the lottery burning MWALI does not quietly re-authorise minting it again.

== Why it is separate from KULA ==

Separating the two lets a liquidity position be counted and governed in its own right rather than existing as a side effect of a reward programme. MWALI can be paired back into KULA, used as governance weight, or wired into further gauges without touching KULA's capped emission schedule. It is also what makes the lottery a real sink: MWALI is burned for tickets while the prize is paid in KULA, so supply actually leaves. See [[Proof of Liquidity]] for the full argument.

== Current state ==

MWALI '''is''' minting. All five pools are staked and accruing, and the token trades against KULA in a pool of its own. A previous revision of this page reported zero supply and blamed a gauge misconfigured to pay KULA — that described the old gauge and the old token, both superseded.
